name: Frenotomy / tongue tie release for face

card.summary: Surgical release of the tongue's frenulum, discussed online as a step toward better tongue posture and jaw development; studies cover feeding and speech, not facial appearance.
card.aka: Frenectomy, frenuloplasty, tongue-tie release, ankyloglossia release
card.note: Evidence for facial or jaw changes from tongue-tie release is absent; documented benefits are studied for infant feeding and some speech outcomes, and rare major complications are reported.

quick.overview:
Tongue-tie (ankyloglossia) is a condition in which the band of tissue under the tongue limits its movement. Releasing it is a short procedure called a frenotomy or frenectomy. Some online discussions of jaw and face development link tongue posture and tongue-tie release to appearance.

Published research examines breastfeeding, speech and sleep outcomes. No study found tests the procedure for changing facial structure in adults or children.
quick.mechanism: The procedure cuts or reshapes the lingual frenulum, sometimes with a laser, to increase tongue mobility. Proponents of the facial link argue that a freer tongue can rest against the palate; Wikipedia notes this posture is associated with nasal breathing and that associations with palate and jaw development are presented as hypotheses.
quick.risks: Reviews describe the procedure as simple with low complication rates in infants, but case reports and a systematic review document major complications after tongue-tie release. Experts disagree about how often tongue-tie causes problems and about diagnosis, particularly of posterior tongue-tie.

lead: Frenotomy, also called frenectomy or frenuloplasty, is the surgical release of the lingual frenulum in people with tongue-tie (ankyloglossia). It is established for some infants with breastfeeding difficulty, and its use for speech, sleep and other outcomes is debated. [1][2]

Appearance-focused communities discuss tongue-tie release as part of a story about tongue posture and jaw development: the idea is that a tongue free to rest on the palate supports nasal breathing and palate width, which in turn is linked to a more forward, defined lower face. Wikipedia describes associations between ankyloglossia and a narrow high palate, open bite and mouth breathing, framed as associations and hypotheses. [3] No published human study has tested frenotomy as a way of changing facial structure. [3]

Systematic reviews report mixed evidence on speech outcomes, and a scoping review of non-infants found improvements in tongue movement with treatment, while noting that definitions and diagnostic criteria for tongue-tie are not generally agreed. [4][5][6] Adults and children who seek release for tongue mobility, speech or oral function describe it as a short outpatient procedure under local anesthesia. [3]
infobox: Frenotomy, frenectomy, frenuloplasty; scalpel, scissors or CO2 laser [3]

paras: Wikipedia describes ankyloglossia as a restrictive lingual frenulum that limits tongue movement, ranging from mild bands to complete tethering, with no generally accepted definition, classification or diagnostic parameters as of 2025. It reports that treatment is usually a quick frenotomy or frenuloplasty under local anesthesia, sometimes with a CO2 laser. [3] It states that the cause is unknown, that it may be heritable, and that it has been associated with rare syndromes. [3]

Professionals disagree on how often tongue-tie causes symptoms. Some consider it rarely symptomatic, while others link it to many issues. [3] A 2017 JAMA Otolaryngology review noted wide variation in practice, a lack of high-quality studies and an undocumented natural history of untreated ankyloglossia, and called for consistent terminology and uniform grading such as the Hazelbaker tool and Coryllos grading. [18] Diagnosis depends on tongue range of motion rather than appearance, and in children a wait-and-see approach is common because the frenulum may recede between about six months and six years of age, according to Wikipedia. [3]

A frenotomy divides the frenulum with scissors, a scalpel or a laser; a frenuloplasty also closes the wound in a way intended to lengthen the tissue. [3] Reported trials have compared diode laser with scalpel in infants. [19] Orofacial myofunctional therapy is discussed in the literature as an adjunct intended to reduce tissue reattachment and retrain tongue function, and Wikipedia lists myology exercises as a non-surgical option. [3][14] The 2020 American Academy of Otolaryngology-Head and Neck Surgery consensus statement grouped expert opinion on indications, informed consent, procedure and older children, with 41 of 89 statements reaching consensus after three Delphi rounds. [20]

sections.h: Reported links to jaw and face
paras: Wikipedia presents several associations between ankyloglossia and dental or jaw features, including open bite, a narrow high palate, tongue thrusting, crowding and temporomandibular pain, framing these as associations and hypotheses. [3] A tongue resting on the palate is described as supporting nasal breathing, and mouth breathing is in turn associated with sleep-disordered breathing. [3] The article does not discuss mewing or facial aesthetics. [3]

In looksmaxxing discussion, tongue-tie release is sometimes mentioned next to mewing and palate expansion as a way of allowing proper tongue posture. Practitioners in this area say that untethering the tongue is a prerequisite for the posture they advocate, while the published literature on frenotomy addresses feeding, speech and oral function rather than facial skeletal change. A 2022 systematic review of the upper lip frenulum and midline gap between teeth noted that parental exposure to online advice about feeding and long-term aesthetic concerns may encourage frenectomies and found no consensus on benefit for preventing the gap. [21]

Mewing is oral posture training in which the tongue is pressed against the roof of the mouth, named for British orthodontist John Mew and developed with his son Mike as part of orthotropics; Wikipedia reports interest rising from January 2019 and viral spread on YouTube and TikTok, especially in looksmaxxing communities. [28] The American Association of Orthodontists says there is no evidence that mewing improves the jaw, and Wikipedia reports that Mike Mew was struck from the UK dental register in 2024. [28] Wikipedia's mewing article does not mention tongue-tie, so the link between release surgery and mewing is made in community discussion rather than in that reference. [28]

For infants, the 2017 Cochrane review addressed frenotomy and feeding in infants under three months, noting tongue-tie is present in 4% to 11% of newborns, [2] and a 2024 meta-analysis of 21 studies reported improvements in breastfeeding self-efficacy, nipple pain and infant reflux severity after frenotomy. [22] Randomised trials include the UK FROSTTIE trial of frenotomy plus breastfeeding support versus support alone [23] and a 2025 double-blind randomised trial in newborns. [24]

A 2015 structured review described wide variation in reported prevalence (0.02 to 10.7%) and noted the subjectivity of the outcome measures used to judge whether tongue-tie division helps breastfeeding. [7] A 2019 review said surgical intervention should be reserved for symptomatic ankyloglossia and that frenulotomy is simple with low risk of complications. [8]

A 2024 systematic review and meta-analysis examined speech outcomes after frenectomy in children. [9] A 2013 systematic review looked at breastfeeding and speech articulation. [10] A 2022 scoping review of non-infants found that most treatment options significantly improved the anatomical limitation of the tongue. [5] A 2023 scoping review of children beyond infancy identified symptoms that may be partly attributable to ankyloglossia. [11] Wikipedia notes later reviews arguing speech sound development is not affected, and says adults in a small study reported difficulty with kissing, licking lips and eating ice cream, and teasing. [3]

No studies found that examine frenotomy or tongue-tie release for facial appearance or jaw structure. Studies of tongue-tie release address breastfeeding, speech and quality-of-life outcomes. [4][5][11] A prospective cohort of 37 children (mean age 4.2 years) who had CO2 laser frenectomy plus myofunctional exercises reported improvements in speech in 89%, along with feeding and sleep outcomes, using parent questionnaires. [12] A randomised trial of frenotomy for posterior tongue-tie used objective measures, and a later response article discussed it. [25][26]

A case report and systematic review described major complications after tongue-tie release and noted that complications are thought to be low but are not well reported or studied; it also reported a more than tenfold increase in diagnoses and frenotomies in the US from 1997 to 2012. [13] A New Zealand programme aimed to reduce the rate of newborn release surgery while supporting breastfeeding. [27] Wikipedia mentions post-operative pain in some adults, an uncited claim. [3] Myofunctional therapy is discussed in the literature as an adjunct to reduce tissue reattachment. [14]

timeline.event: Reported over tenfold rise in tongue-tie diagnoses and frenotomies in the US. [13]
Structured review on tongue-tie and breastfeeding published. [7]
Cochrane review of frenotomy for tongue-tie in newborn infants published. [2]
US otolaryngology consensus statement on ankyloglossia in children. [20]

Google Trends interest in mewing begins rising, followed by viral spread on social media. [28]
Mike Mew is struck from the UK dental register, as reported by Wikipedia. [28]

lore.intro: In appearance-focused communities, tongue-tie release is discussed as a possible enabler of tongue posture practices such as mewing, alongside palate expansion and nasal breathing. [28]

claims.claim: A tongue-tie stops the tongue resting on the palate, so release is needed for proper tongue posture
claims.believers: Posture advocates say a tethered tongue cannot rest against the roof of the mouth, so untethering is a first step toward the facial changes they attribute to tongue posture. [28]
claims.experts: Wikipedia describes ankyloglossia as a restriction of tongue movement with no generally accepted diagnostic criteria, and lists tongue posture and palate links as associations and hypotheses. [3]

claims.claim: Tongue posture can reshape the jaws and face
claims.believers: Proponents of mewing and orthotropics say pressing the tongue to the palate improves jaw and facial structure. [28]
claims.experts: The American Association of Orthodontists says there is no evidence that mewing improves the jaw, and the Wikipedia article reports no credible research showing orthotropics is effective. [28]

claims.claim: A narrow palate and mouth breathing are linked to tongue-tie
claims.believers: Practitioners cite open bite, high narrow palate and mouth breathing as consequences of restricted tongue movement. [3]
claims.experts: Wikipedia presents these as associations and hypotheses, and notes professionals disagree on how often tongue-tie causes symptoms. [3]

claims.claim: Release in infancy or later improves feeding, speech and sleep
claims.believers: Clinics offering release, and parent reports in cohort studies, describe improved feeding, speech and sleep afterward. [12]
claims.experts: Meta-analyses report improved breastfeeding outcomes in infants, while speech reviews are mixed and a consensus statement found agreement on only 41 of 89 statements. [22][9][20]

claims.claim: Tongue-tie release is a low-risk, quick procedure
claims.believers: Reviews describe frenulotomy as simple with a low complication rate in infants. [8]
claims.experts: A case report and systematic review documented major complications after release and noted complications are not well reported. [13]
